propositions.text: Teva Canada Limited moves to strike Gilead's statement of claim for insufficient material facts for past infringement and quia timet claim
Gilead argues its pleaded facts are sufficient or should be allowed to amend with discovery facts from separate action
Gilead seeks relief from implied undertaking rule to use discovery information for this litigation

paragraphs.summary: Teva moves to strike Gilead's claim for insufficient facts; Gilead argues sufficiency or amendment and seeks relief from implied undertaking rule.

propositions.text: Both motions agreed to be heard together
Gilead should be relieved of implied undertaking rule
Gilead's current statement of claim fails to support past or current infringement; proposed amendments not permitted
Current statement of claim fails for quia timet claim but proposed amendments plus particulars would suffice; Gilead may amend

paragraphs.summary: Motions heard together; court relieves Gilead from implied undertaking, strikes claim for past infringement, allows amendment for quia timet claim.

propositions.text: Teva designated discovery information confidential under protective order
Protective order governs treatment of exchanged information but not automatic sealing
Teva moves for confidentiality order for discovery information
If Gilead's motion dismissed, implied undertaking rule alone justifies confidentiality order
If Gilead relieved of implied undertaking, Teva's evidence insufficient to support confidentiality order
Teva only showed it treated info confidentially, not that disclosure would cause serious harm
Teva abandons confidentiality motion
Discovery information remains under seal until appeals exhausted to protect against premature disclosure
Court avoids discussing specifics of discovery information to protect confidentiality
General nature of information disclosed is sufficient for reasons to be intelligible

paragraphs.summary: Teva designated discovery info confidential; confidentiality order motion abandoned; info remains sealed pending appeals; court avoids specifics.

propositions.text: Action involves Canadian patents 059 and 619 owned by Gilead covering TDF and TD
Gilead markets antiviral drugs under trademarks TRUVADA, ATRIPLA, VIREAD
059 Patent expires July 23, 2018; 619 Patent expires July 25, 2017

paragraphs.summary: Action concerns Gilead's 059 and 619 patents on antiviral drugs marketed as TRUVADA, ATRIPLA, VIREAD with specified expiry dates.

propositions.text: Teva served Notices of Allegation in 2011-2012 alleging invalidity of patents but not non-infringement
Gilead responded by applications under Patented Medicines Regulations to prohibit Minister issuing NOCs to Teva until patent expiry

paragraphs.summary: Teva alleged patent invalidity in Notices; Gilead sought orders to prohibit Minister issuing NOCs to Teva until patent expiry.

propositions.text: Teva filed action T-1529-12 seeking declaration patents invalid, alleging interest to import, make, use, sell TDF products
That action did not allege non-infringement but alleged Teva's interest in marketing TDF products
Discovery transcripts Gilead seeks to use were from that action in October 2013 after prohibition hearing but before judgment

paragraphs.summary: Teva filed invalidity action alleging interest to market TDF; discovery transcripts from that action sought for use by Gilead.

propositions.text: Court prohibited Minister from issuing NOC to Teva until 619 Patent expiry but dismissed applications for 059 Patent
Minister could issue NOCs to Teva as early as July 25, 2017, expiry of 619 Patent

paragraphs.summary: Court barred NOC issuance to Teva until 619 Patent expiry but allowed NOCs after July 25, 2017; 059 Patent applications dismissed.

propositions.text: Teva continued impeachment action T-1529-12 for both patents; trial set for March 2, 2015
Discoveries and expert reports exchanged in 2014
Teva served notice of discontinuance for 059 Patent only on December 17, 2014; pleadings not amended

paragraphs.summary: Teva continued impeachment action with trial set for 2015; discontinued 059 Patent claim in late 2014 without amending pleadings.

propositions.text: Trial adjourned from March 2, 2015 to November 28, 2016 due to serious illness of Teva's expert witness

paragraphs.summary: Trial delayed to November 2016 due to serious illness of Teva's expert witness.

propositions.text: Gilead instituted present action November 9, 2015 seeking declaration of past and future infringement of 059 Patent
Teva demanded particulars of past, current, and future infringement allegations
Gilead declined to provide further particulars, prompting Teva's motion to strike

paragraphs.summary: Gilead sued for infringement; Teva demanded particulars; Gilead declined; Teva moved to strike claim.

propositions.text: Gilead filed motion to consolidate present action with T-1529-12 for joint hearing in November 2016
Consolidation motion scheduled for hearing if Gilead's action survives motion to strike

paragraphs.summary: Gilead seeks consolidation of actions for joint hearing if claim survives motion to strike.

propositions.text: Gilead alleges Teva intends to import, make, use, sell TDF products before 059 Patent expiry
Teva's motion to strike challenges Gilead to plead specific material facts or face striking
Gilead wishes to use discovery transcript from T-1529-12 to meet pleading challenge

paragraphs.summary: Gilead alleges Teva's intent to market TDF early; Teva challenges pleading; Gilead seeks to use prior discovery transcript.

propositions.text: Teva alleges in T-1529-12 it is interested person intending to market TDF products and must impeach claims or succeed under PM (NOC) Regulations
Discoveries addressed Teva's intentions and actions including approvability status with Minister of Health

paragraphs.summary: Teva alleged intent to market TDF and need to impeach claims or succeed under regulations; discovery covered intentions and approvals.

propositions.text: Implied undertaking rule prevents use of discovery info outside litigation in which disclosed
Rule protects privacy of examinees and encourages candid discovery balancing public interest and rights
Juman v Doucette and Sanofi-Aventis cases cited for rationale and exceptions to implied undertaking rule
Court may relieve persons from implied undertaking rule in interest of justice

paragraphs.summary: Implied undertaking rule limits discovery use to litigation; protects privacy and candor; court may relieve in interest of justice.

propositions.text: Juman v Doucette requires applicant to show public interest outweighing implied undertaking values on balance of probabilities
Teva argues Juman sets higher standard than prior courts
Court disagrees; Supreme Court recognizes existing provincial rules and flexible categories of public interest

paragraphs.summary: Juman requires public interest outweighing implied undertaking; Teva claims higher standard; court disagrees and notes flexibility.

propositions.text: Superior public interest includes contradictory testimony in different proceedings per Juman
Witnesses should not be allowed to tailor evidence to suit needs in each proceeding
Gilead argues same public interest applies to party litigation positions, not just witness testimony
Court agrees with Gilead that public interest applies to party litigation positions

paragraphs.summary: Juman recognizes public interest against contradictory testimony; Gilead argues applies to party positions; court agrees.

propositions.text: Teva publicly alleged intent to market TDF before patent expiry in T-1529-12
Facts disclosed on discovery supported Teva's allegations and advanced its interests
Teva now argues Gilead cannot prove intent to launch TDF and lacks material facts
Gilead says Teva relies on implied undertaking rule to deny evidence it gave supporting intent
Implied undertaking would allow Teva to tailor litigation positions and play games with justice

paragraphs.summary: Teva alleged intent to market TDF and disclosed facts; now denies basis; Gilead says implied undertaking enables Teva to game justice.

propositions.text: Circumstances differ from Juman and other cases where discovery was reluctantly provided
Here, discovery supported voluntary factual allegations by Teva for its own interest
Had Teva refused discovery, sanction likely would be inability to introduce evidence without leave, not striking pleadings
Teva requested Gilead admit its status as interested person and served will say statement of intent to market TDF

paragraphs.summary: Unlike Juman, discovery here was voluntary to support Teva's allegations; refusal would limit evidence, not strike pleadings; Teva confirmed intent.

propositions.text: Discovery evidence likely would have been disclosed even without implied undertaking rule as it advanced Teva's case
Teva confirmed intent to present such evidence at trial in will-say statement
Upholding implied undertaking would delay disclosure and Gilead's use of evidence
Teva uses implied undertaking to play games by asserting intent in one proceeding and denying basis in another
Public interest in preventing misuse of implied undertaking outweighs its protective values here
Teva was not a reluctant litigant needing protection of implied undertaking

paragraphs.summary: Discovery evidence would be disclosed anyway; Teva confirmed intent; implied undertaking delays disclosure; court finds public interest favors relief.

propositions.text: Juman states discovery material used in another action with same or similar parties and issues generally granted leave
Additional plaintiffs are similar parties claiming under patentee per Patent Act
Present action is related though different cause of action; issue of Teva's intent is the same
Teva cannot claim actions are distinct because 059 Patent no longer at issue in T-1529-12

paragraphs.summary: Juman allows use of discovery in related actions with similar parties; present action parties and issues are similar; Teva's distinction rejected.

propositions.text: Gilead's statement of claim vaguely alleges past or current infringement by Teva importing or manufacturing TDF.
Teva sought particulars of facts supporting Gilead's infringement allegations but was refused.
Case law states infringement actions lacking sufficient material facts and relying on bald conclusions or regulatory approval are abuse of process and should be struck.

paragraphs.summary: Gilead alleges vague past or current infringement; Teva sought particulars but was refused; case law says vague infringement claims relying on bald conclusions should be struck.

propositions.text: Gilead's allegations of past or current infringement must be struck as plain and obvious.
Whether Gilead's proposed amendments to cure the defect should be allowed.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Gilead's past or current infringement allegations must be struck and considers if proposed amendments should be allowed.

propositions.text: Proposed amendments relying on Teva's intention to enter market and stockpile product are speculative and not reasonably based on evidence.
No reasonable basis to infer Teva made or stockpiled commercial infringing product in Canada.
Availability of product is not synonymous with actual possession; prior cases distinguish these facts.
Proposed amendments amount to bald speculation and should not be allowed.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds proposed amendments based on Teva's intention and stockpiling are speculative and should not be allowed.

propositions.text: Proposed amendments pleading admissions of infringement mischaracterize discovery evidence and should not be allowed.
Discovery shows Teva admitted only regulatory preparation activities exempted by Patent Act section 55.2.
Such conduct is insufficient to sustain an action for past or current infringement (Eli Lilly v Nu-Pharm).

paragraphs.summary: Court finds proposed amendments pleading admissions mischaracterize evidence; Teva admitted only exempt regulatory activities insufficient for infringement claim.

propositions.text: Criteria for quia timet patent infringement claim require deliberate expressed intention, imminence, substantial harm, and cogent facts (Connaught Laboratories).

paragraphs.summary: Court states criteria for quia timet patent infringement claims from Connaught Laboratories.

propositions.text: Gilead's claim relies on Teva's expressed intention to market TDF before patent expiry and procedural circumstances.
Gilead's claim is silent on Teva's ability to carry out intention, including ANDS approvability status.
Similar to prior case where expressed intention met but temporal imminence failed due to lack of approvability allegations.
Teva argues timing of market entry is speculative and contingent on obtaining NOC from Health Canada.
Pfizer v Lilly held that lack of NOC approval makes imminence speculative.

paragraphs.summary: Gilead alleges Teva's intention to market TDF but omits approvability; court finds claim similar to prior case failing imminence; Teva argues timing speculative without NOC.

propositions.text: Without amendments, Gilead's claim alleges deliberate intention raising strong possibility of infringement.
Claim lacks material facts showing infringement is imminent; remains speculative without NOC approvability allegations.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Gilead's claim alleges intention but lacks material facts to show imminent infringement without NOC approvability allegations.

propositions.text: Discovery evidence and proposed amendments are cogent, precise and material to satisfy imminence criterion.
Gilead should be allowed to make proposed amendments.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds discovery evidence and proposed amendments satisfy imminence criterion and allows Gilead to amend claim.

propositions.text: If not relieved of implied undertaking rule, Gilead argues facts permit inference that Teva's ANDS submissions are approvable and on patent hold.
Court agrees these facts form cogent, precise and material basis to infer Teva's ANDS is on patent hold awaiting patent expiry or impeachment.
Even if discovery evidence not allowed, Gilead could amend pleadings to raise these circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: Gilead argues facts infer Teva's ANDS approvable and on patent hold; court agrees and would allow amendment even without discovery evidence.

propositions.text: Plaintiff need only plead a reasonably arguable case; motions to strike should not require proof of case at pleading stage.

paragraphs.summary: Court states plaintiff need only plead a reasonably arguable case; motions to strike should not require proof at pleading stage.

propositions.text: Probability of infringement in July 2017 is sufficiently imminent to justify quia timet action.
Quia timet actions aim to stop events before they happen; initiating 22 months prior is not premature or pointless.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds infringement probability in July 2017 sufficiently imminent; quia timet actions can be initiated well before event to be avoided.

propositions.text: Substantial harm suffices for quia timet claim; irreparable harm is not required; case law offers no further guidance.

paragraphs.summary: Court states substantial harm suffices for quia timet claim; irreparable harm not required; no further case law guidance.

propositions.text: Current statement of claim alleges deprivation of exclusivity, damages over $50,000, and Teva's profit.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes current claim alleges loss of exclusivity, damages over $50,000, and Teva's profit.

propositions.text: Deprivation of exclusivity alone is not substantial or irreparable harm per Connaught Laboratories.
Infringer's profits do not necessarily constitute harm to patentee.
Only remaining harm allegation is damages over $50,000, which is not precise or cogent enough.
Proposed amendments lack further particulars on magnitude of expected loss.
Gilead should be allowed to amend claim to particularize damages; Teva may argue insufficiency of particulars.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds current harm allegations insufficient; allows Gilead to amend claim to particularize damages; Teva may challenge sufficiency.

propositions.text: Gilead is relieved of implied undertaking rule for certain discovery transcripts.
Discovery transcripts remain sealed until all appeals exhausted unless court orders otherwise.
Gilead's claim alleging past or current infringement is struck without leave to amend.
Gilead shall amend claim to remove past or current infringement allegations and add proposed amendments except specified parts.
Gilead shall amend claim to add particulars of expected damages if Teva enters market before patent expiry.
Teva may reapply to strike claim if particulars fail to allege sufficient material facts of substantial harm.
Gilead shall have costs of motion to be relieved of implied undertaking rule; no costs on motion to strike as success divided.

paragraphs.summary: Court orders Gilead relieved of implied undertaking rule, discovery sealed, past infringement claim struck, amendments required, and costs awarded accordingly.
